_comment: Mutation testing. `npm run test:mutation`, and see README.md for what it is for.
The question coverage cannot ask. Coverage asks whether a line ran; mutation asks
whether anything would have noticed it being wrong. A test that renders a component
and asserts nothing about it takes the coverage of every line it touched to 100%, and
this repository has both halves of that already: a test named for a guard it cannot
reach, and an off-by-one on a line reported at 100% statements.
Scope. `packages/shared` is the pure logic and the small surface, plus the two files in
`packages/ui` that are logic rather than markup. The 83 component files are out on
purpose: mutating a className string produces survivors by the hundred, all of them
the mutation score punishing a design system for having strings in it.
The whole suite runs, and that is what makes this the measurement rather than a proxy.
packages/shared scores 90% statements under its own project and 100% under the full run,
because customers.ts, navigation.ts and reports.ts are covered second-hand through apps/api
and apps/web. It costs 81 minutes at ~77 tests per mutant, which is why it is a CI job of
its own and why there is a five-minute proxy beside it — `npm run test:mutation:fast`,
stryker.fast.config.json, and vitest.mutation.config.ts, which measures what that costs.
inPlace, and it is not optional here. Stryker's default is to copy the repository into a
sandbox and mutate the copy. This is an npm-workspaces monorepo, so node_modules/@support-desk/*
are symlinks pointing back out at packages/ and apps/ — which means every test that imports
@support-desk/shared runs against the ORIGINAL file and never sees the mutant. The first full
run scored 39% with 186 mutants reported as having no coverage, including every mutant in
reports.ts, a file the API suite exercises on three routes. That number was not a weak test
suite; it was a sensor measuring the wrong copy of the code, and it is exactly the sort of
confidently-wrong figure a harness is supposed to stop rather than produce.
In place, reports.ts goes from 0% with 30 uncovered to 93% with two survivors. The cost is
real: Stryker edits the working tree and restores it from .stryker-tmp/backup-* when it
finishes, so a run killed halfway leaves mutants in the source. Run it on a clean tree.
The threshold is set from the first run rather than chosen, the same way the four counting
rules in eslint.config.js were set just above the worst function in the repository. The
first clean run scored 84.39%. `break` is 82 rather than 84 because a handful of mutants in
workflow.ts time out rather than being killed outright — a mutated transition table can make
the reachability test loop — and a timeout is scored as killed, so the total moves a point or
so between runs. Two points of slack, and the ratchet is lowering it, not raising it.
This is the slowest thing in the repository: ~77 tests per mutant, because packages/shared is
imported by the whole web suite. It is a CI job of its own and it is not in the agent hook.
dryRunTimeoutMinutes is raised from the default 5 because the initial pass runs all 703
tests once, instrumented for per-test coverage, and that is what makes the per-mutant runs
cheap afterwards. It timed out at the default and Stryker's message for that — 'something
went wrong in the initial test run' — does not say so.
